messages:
maria_g: Heads-up — I'm going to swap the overlay branch for staging from `staging-old` -> `staging-new` later today. There's a Terraform change in the PR that renames secret paths (team-secrets -> infra-secrets). Quick Q: will that break the staging canary or any CI jobs that mount the old paths? PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4823

sam_k: Can you paste the PR number? I can run a local `terraform plan` against the staging workspace. Also pinging @lee_t for k8s overlay impacts.

maria_g: PR is #4823 — thanks. It's a small rename and a service port tweak in the k8s overlay. Terraform plan snippet from the branch:```
  # aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.app_secret will be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "app_secret" {
+    ~ secret_id     = "arn:aws:secretsmanager:...:secret:team-secrets-abc" -> "arn:aws:secretsmanager:...:secret:infra-secrets-abc"
      ~ secret_string = jsonencode({
          ~ "DB_PASSWORD" = (sensitive) -> (sensitive)
        })
  }
```

devops-bot: CI /prs/4823 pipeline finished: success ✅ — plan shows secret rename and no deletion of resources, plan requires manual apply.

lee_t: The k8s overlay changes look like a port rename on the `api` svc from 8080 -> 8081 and a readinessProbe path change. That means the container will re-deploy but should be fine if probe matches. Need to confirm any podDisruptionBudget or HPA settings that assume same port.

jonah_r: FYI the staging deploy job mounts `secret://team-secrets/infra` in one place (legacy mapping). If we flip paths, the legacy mount will 404. Suggest either: 1) add a short-lived compatibility secret with the old name; or 2) change the deployment manifest to reference both keys (mount two envFroms or a projected volume) for a couple of deploy cycles.

maria_g: Good call. I prefer option 2 (manifest side fix) to avoid creating duplicate secrets. @sam_k can you share the minimal k8s patch we should apply as a canary to have both paths available?

sam_k: Sure — quick projected volume approach (canary only):```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: api-canary
spec:
  containers:
  - name: api
    image: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/api:canary
    envFrom:
    - secretRef:
        name: infra-secrets
    - secretRef:
        name: team-secrets
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8081
```
This keeps both names available for the app env. We'll remove `team-secrets` after a full roll.

lee_t: Also add a canary TrafficSplit or header-based routing so only 10% of traffic hits the canary. If using our service mesh we can do:```bash
kubectl apply -f traffic-split-canary.yaml
```
I'll draft the canary overlay in a branch and push in ~15m.

maria_g: Thanks. Can we schedule the promote at 23:30 UTC? I want a 15-minute manual canary window then full promote. If anything looks off we roll back.

jonah_r: Works for me. I will update the staging deploy job to preserve the `team-secrets` mount for one more deploy cycle so old CI jobs don't break (non-prod-only). That avoids an immediate outage for any long-running jobs.

sam_k: I ran `terraform plan -var-file=staging.tfvars` locally — no resource replacements except the secret_version replacement (no data loss). Approving the PR from infra perspective.

lee_t: Pushed the canary overlay branch: `overlay/staging-canary-secret-compat`. It contains the projected envFrom and a TrafficSplit with 10% weight. Will open the k8s PR in a minute.

maria_g: Opening the promote window at 23:30 UTC. Please be ready to rollback. Thanks for the quick checks everyone. :thumbsup: 

sam_k: LGTM, will monitor terraform apply logs.

devops-bot: Reminder: scheduled deploy at 23:30 UTC -> pipeline will trigger 23:25 UTC for canary checks.

jonah_r: After promote we should run a quick smoke: `curl -sS -I https://staging.api.redwood.example/health | head -n 1` and a secret lookup test via the debug job.

lee_t: I'll watch metrics and probe failures. If readiness rate drops >5% in the first 5m I will rollback.

maria_g: Awesome — closing out. If any last-minute blockers reply here.
